title: Polynomial-time closure under Boolean disjunction
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean-valued functions on bit strings. If the one-bit output functions $x\mapsto p(x)$ and $x\mapsto q(x)$ are both polynomial-time computable, then the function sending $x$ to the one-bit word $1$ when at least one of $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ equals $1$, and to $0$ otherwise, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ and $q$ are functions from bit strings to Boolean values.
The one-bit output function $x\mapsto p(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
The one-bit output function $x\mapsto q(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
